quickAnswer: Türkiye treated nearly 1.4 million international health visitors in 2025, drawing patients for hair restoration, dentistry, aesthetics, ophthalmology and bariatric surgery at 40% to 65% below UK and US private fees. Safe planning in 2026 means separating clinical decisions from travel logistics and verifying every clinic independently before paying a deposit.
category: Medical Travel to Türkiye — Independent Advisory & Safety (The ITO Standard)

body.text: Why do over a million international patients travel to Türkiye each year?

International patients choose Türkiye for a rare combination of short waiting times, high-volume specialist hospitals, direct flights from Europe, the UK and North America, and transparent self-pay pricing. Official TurkStat and USHAŞ figures recorded 1,398,580 health visitors spending USD 3.02 billion in 2025, following 1.51 million visitors in 2024.

Volume alone does not guarantee uniform quality, and recent data shows the market maturing. According to [official TurkStat health tourism data](https://clinicprof.com/turkey-health-tourism-statistics/) and [USHAŞ visitor counts](https://medicaltourismwatch.com/turkiye-medical-tourism-fewer-patients-higher-fees/), patient numbers dipped slightly from the 2023 peak of 1.54 million while total spending held steady above USD 3 billion—a sign that patients are shifting away from cut-price bargain deals toward established private hospitals. State oversight via [USHAŞ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USHA%C5%9E) and the [Ministry of Health's authorized provider registry](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) alongside internationally audited [JCI-accredited hospitals](https://digitalassets.jointcommission.org/api/public/content/assets/3/7/ebjcih24_sample_pages.pdf) gives patients verifiable benchmarks if they know where to look.
Which specialties (hair, dental, aesthetic, eye, bariatric) are strongest?

Türkiye's strongest international medical specialties are hair transplantation (FUE and DHI), restorative and cosmetic dentistry, plastic and reconstructive surgery, refractive eye procedures (LASIK and lens replacement), and bariatric surgery. High annual case volume allows specialist teams in Istanbul, Izmir and Antalya to invest in modern diagnostic and surgical equipment.
Each specialty carries distinct logistics and recovery timelines that marketing packages often gloss over:

items: Hair restoration: Typically requires 3 to 4 nights in Istanbul, with day-two wash checks and careful sun and impact protection on flights home.
Dental implants and crowns: Simple veneers or crowns may take 5 to 7 days, while two-stage implants require a healing gap of 3 to 6 months between surgical placement and final prosthetics.
Aesthetic and plastic surgery: Demands full hospital operating theatres, board-certified plastic surgeons and 7 to 14 nights of supervised post-operative recovery before long-haul flights.
Ophthalmology (LASIK / cataract / lens): Fast outpatient procedures with 24-hour and 72-hour slit-lamp follow-ups.
Bariatric surgery (gastric sleeve): Requires pre-operative multidisciplinary screening, inpatient hospital monitoring and strict fit-to-fly clearance.

body.text: How do realistic 2026 costs compare to the UK, US and Germany?

Across 75 tracked procedures in 2026, Turkish international guide prices average roughly 40% below UK private ranges and 56% below US self-pay fees, with the sharpest savings in hair restoration and full-arch dentistry. Factoring in flights, recovery-appropriate hotels and a companion still leaves substantial net savings on major elective procedures.

Published 2026 benchmarks from the [Turkey Medical Price Index](https://acibademinternational.com/price-index/) and European [hair transplant cost comparisons](https://www.metropolmed.com/blog/hair-transplant-cost-turkey-vs-europe/) highlight realistic spreads—and also show why rock-bottom ads should trigger caution. Ultra-cheap quotes often exclude pre-op blood panels, hospital overnight stays, revision policies or named-surgeon fees.
Figures are indicative 2026 market ranges for comparison only; final clinical quotes depend on medical assessment by a licensed physician.
What is the role of an independent coordinator vs a clinic salesperson?

A clinic salesperson or commission-funded medical agency is paid to convert your enquiry into a booking for a specific provider, whereas an independent, client-paid coordinator works solely for you—organising recovery-ready hotels, airport transfers, companion logistics and scheduling without taking kickbacks from any hospital or clinic.

That financial boundary changes every conversation. Commission agents earn 15% to 35% of your surgical fee, creating an obvious incentive to rush deposits or steer you toward high-margin clinics rather than the right clinical fit. faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye recommend specific clinics or doctors?
faq.a: No. We never recommend clinics on commission or give clinical advice. We coordinate your visit—hotels, transfers, companion plans and recovery logistics—while your licensed medical team makes all clinical decisions.

faq.q: How many days should I stay in Türkiye after surgery?
faq.a: Stay durations depend on your surgeon's fit-to-fly clearance, typically 3 to 4 nights for hair restoration, 5 to 7 nights for dental crowns, and 7 to 14 nights for aesthetic or bariatric surgery.

faq.q: Why are medical procedures cheaper in Türkiye than in the UK or US?
faq.a: Lower hospital overhead, domestic staff costs, favourable exchange rates and high specialist case volumes drive lower prices—not lower clinical standards at properly accredited hospitals.

faq.q: Does standard travel insurance cover medical tourism complications?
faq.a: Usually no. Most standard travel policies exclude elective medical procedures and related complications; patients should check specialist medical-travel complication cover before flying.

faq.q: Is it safe to combine sightseeing with a medical trip to Türkiye?
faq.a: Light sightseeing works best before your procedure, not after. Post-procedure days should prioritise rest, quiet recovery hotels and proximity to your hospital for follow-up checks.

faq.q: Should I send medical photos or records in my first enquiry to a travel coordinator?
faq.a: No. Never send passport scans, medical records, diagnostic photos or payment details in an initial travel enquiry; share clinical records only directly with your chosen licensed medical provider via secure channels.
